_readme: Human-reviewed source of truth for tariff measures. See README.md for the schema and editing rules. Every entry cites primary or reputable secondary sources and carries the date it was last verified against them.

actions.title: Section 232 tariffs on steel (25%) and aluminum (10%)
actions.rateNote: 25% steel, 10% aluminum. Canada and Mexico exempted May 2019; Argentina/Brazil/Korea/Australia quotas; EU/Japan/UK tariff-rate quotas from 2022
actions.notes: Superseded by the March 2025 proclamations that ended all country exemptions and quotas.

actions.title: Section 301 tariffs on Chinese goods (Lists 1–4A and four-year review)
actions.rateNote: 7.5% (List 4A) to 25% (Lists 1–3); four-year review raised EVs to 100%, semiconductors and solar cells to 50%, batteries and steel/aluminum to 25% (2024–2026)
actions.hsLabel: machinery, electronics, vehicles, chemicals, metals and more

actions.title: IEEPA 'fentanyl' tariff on Chinese goods
actions.notes: Held unlawful by the Supreme Court in Learning Resources v. Trump (Feb 20, 2026); collection ended Feb 24, 2026; refunds via CBP's CAPE process.

actions.title: IEEPA 'fentanyl' tariff on Canadian goods
actions.rateNote: 10% on energy and potash

actions.title: IEEPA 'fentanyl' tariff on Mexican goods
IEEPA reciprocal tariff on China

rateHistory.note: 34% announced Apr 2, escalated to 125% by Apr 10
Geneva truce; 24% suspended, extended to Nov 2026

actions.title: IEEPA reciprocal baseline tariff (10%)
actions.exemptions: Section 232 goods, pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, energy, certain minerals (Annex II)
actions.notes: Country-specific rates above 10% took effect Aug 7, 2025 (separate entries). Struck down Feb 20, 2026.

actions.title: Reciprocal tariff on EU goods (15% all-in ceiling under the EU–US framework)
Reciprocal tariff on Japan (15% under the US–Japan agreement)
Reciprocal tariff on South Korea (15% under the US–Korea agreement)
Reciprocal tariff on India plus Russian-oil penalty

rateHistory.note: Russian-oil penalty halted under the interim deal; 18% agreed but overtaken by the ruling

actions.title: Reciprocal tariff on Brazil plus 40% surcharge
actions.rateNote: 10% reciprocal + 40% IEEPA surcharge; broad agricultural exclusions added Nov 2025

actions.title: Reciprocal tariff on Switzerland
Reciprocal tariffs on Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka (20%)
Reciprocal tariffs on Southeast and South Asian partners (19%)
Reciprocal tariff on South Africa
Reciprocal tariff on Kazakhstan
Reciprocal tariffs on Türkiye (15%), Israel (17%), Norway (15%) and New Zealand (15%)
actions.rateNote: Israel 17%

actions.title: Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum and derivative products
actions.rateNote: 50% on articles (Annex I-A), 25% on many derivatives (Annex I-B); 200% on Russian aluminum; steel and aluminum duties do not stack on each other
actions.exemptions: EU/Japan/Taiwan civil-aircraft parts; 10% for US-smelted metal

actions.title: Section 232 steel and aluminum tariff on the UK (held at 25%)
actions.rateNote: Stayed at 25% when others rose to 50% on 2025-06-04, under the US–UK Economic Prosperity Deal

actions.title: Section 232 tariffs on automobiles and parts
actions.rateNote: Autos from 2025-04-03, parts from 2025-05-03. USMCA vehicles taxed on non-US content only; USMCA parts exempt
actions.hsLabel: passenger vehicles, light trucks, auto parts
actions.exemptions: USMCA-compliant parts; US content of USMCA vehicles

actions.title: Section 232 auto tariff on EU capped at 15% all-in
actions.rateNote: Additional duty brings the total to 15% (0% additional where the MFN rate is already ≥15%)

actions.title: Section 232 auto tariff on Japan capped at 15% all-in
actions.rateNote: Additional duty brings the total to 15% (0% additional where the MFN rate is already ≥15%)

actions.title: Section 232 auto tariff on South Korea capped at 15% all-in
actions.rateNote: Additional duty brings the total to 15% (0% additional where the MFN rate is already ≥15%)

actions.title: Section 232 auto tariff on Taiwan capped at 15% all-in
actions.rateNote: Additional duty brings the total to 15% (0% additional where the MFN rate is already ≥15%)

actions.title: Section 232 auto tariff on the UK (10% within a 100,000-vehicle quota)
actions.rateNote: 25% above the quota

actions.title: Section 232 tariff on copper and derivative products
actions.rateNote: 50% on semi-finished copper (Annex I-A), 25% on some derivatives; refined cathode excluded

actions.title: Section 232 tariff on softwood timber and lumber
actions.rateNote: Capped so total duty does not exceed 15% from 2026-05-01

actions.title: Section 232 tariffs on upholstered furniture, kitchen cabinets and vanities
actions.rateNote: Rises to 30% (furniture) and 50% (cabinets/vanities) on 2027-01-01

actions.title: Section 232 furniture tariff on deal partners (15% all-in; UK 10%)
Section 232 tariffs on medium- and heavy-duty trucks, buses and parts
actions.rateNote: 25% trucks and parts, 10% buses

actions.title: Section 232 tariff on advanced logic chips
actions.rateNote: Narrow scope: high-performance logic chips and DRAM; broad exemptions for US data centres, R&D, consumer use

actions.title: Section 232 tariff on agricultural and industrial machinery
Section 232 machinery tariff on deal partners capped at 15%
Section 232 tariff on patented pharmaceuticals
actions.rateNote: Tiered 0–100% by origin; 20% for companies with approved US onshoring plans; generics exempt
actions.exemptions: Generic drugs; companies building US plants (Annex II) until 2029

actions.title: Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff on deal partners capped at 15% (UK 10%)
Section 232 tariffs on unmanned aircraft systems
actions.rateNote: 100% on drones over 25 kg, thermal imagers and docking stations; 25% on consumer drones

actions.title: Section 232 drone tariff on deal partners (15% all-in; UK 10%)
Section 232 tariff and minimum import prices on polysilicon, wafers, cells and modules
actions.rateNote: 15% plus minimum import prices ($21/kg polysilicon, $0.38/W modules)

actions.title: Section 122 temporary import surcharge (10%)
actions.rateNote: Announced at 15% on Feb 22 but implemented at 10%; held unlawful by the Court of International Trade on May 7, 2026 (no universal injunction)
actions.exemptions: Section 232 goods; USMCA duty-free goods; CAFTA-DR textiles; ~1,100 Annex II codes
actions.notes: Stop-gap after the IEEPA ruling; 150-day statutory limit. Replaced by the Section 301 forced-labor tariffs.

actions.title: Section 301 forced-labor tariff — tier 1 (10%)
actions.rateNote: Economies with forced-labor import bans or reciprocal trade agreements; also Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Jordan, Trinidad & Tobago
actions.exemptions: Section 232 goods; USMCA duty-free goods; CAFTA-DR and Jordan textiles; civil aircraft; patented pharma; Annex II items
actions.notes: Replaced the Section 122 surcharge on expiry; applies in addition to existing Section 301 duties on China and Brazil.

actions.title: Section 301 forced-labor tariff — tier 2 (10% inclusive of MFN)
actions.rateNote: Additional duty brings the total to 10%
actions.exemptions: Section 232 goods; civil aircraft; patented pharma; Annex II items

actions.title: Section 301 forced-labor tariff — tier 3 (12.5% inclusive of MFN)
actions.rateNote: Additional duty brings the total to 12.5%
actions.exemptions: Section 232 goods; civil aircraft; patented pharma; Annex II items

actions.title: Section 301 forced-labor tariff — tier 4 (12.5%)
actions.rateNote: Also Algeria, Angola, Bahamas, Bahrain, Costa Rica, Dominican Rep., Guyana, Hong Kong, Kuwait, Libya, Nicaragua, Oman, Qatar, Uruguay
actions.exemptions: Section 232 goods; civil aircraft; patented pharma; Annex II items

actions.title: Section 301 tariff on Brazil (digital trade, ethanol, IP, deforestation findings)
actions.exemptions: Section 232 goods; Annex II exclusions (aircraft, orange juice, some energy and agricultural goods)
actions.notes: Brazil said it would invoke its Reciprocity Law and file at the WTO; no countermeasures in force as of verification.

actions.title: Section 338 tariffs on Canadian dairy, alcoholic beverages and motor vehicles (50%)
actions.rateNote: Three proclamations (11046–11048). Scope revised Sept 15, 2026 (cheese, hides, furs, boats, structural steel, aluminum profiles, fasteners, furniture, lighting added) and from that date the 50% stacks on top of Section 232
actions.hsLabel: dairy, beer/wine/spirits, vehicles, structural steel, aluminum profiles, furniture, boats
actions.exemptions: None — USMCA preference does not apply
actions.notes: Signed July 20, 2026; suspended Aug 19–22 during talks, which collapsed Aug 21. First use of Section 338 (Tariff Act of 1930) since the 1930s.

actions.title: Section 338 import bans on Canadian spirits, beer, wine, whey products and large motorcycles
actions.rateNote: Import ban (goods already landed pay the 50% duty instead)

actions.title: Canadian 25% counter-tariff on C$30B of US goods (orange juice, bourbon, appliances, apparel…)
actions.notes: United States Surtax Order (2025). Removed Sept 1, 2025 as Canada aligned with CUSMA-compliant exemptions.

actions.title: Canadian 25% counter-tariff on US steel and aluminum
actions.rateNote: Part of a C$29.8B list; the consumer-goods portion was withdrawn Sept 1, 2025, steel and aluminum remain

actions.title: Canadian 25% counter-tariff on non-CUSMA US vehicles
actions.hsLabel: US-assembled vehicles not meeting CUSMA rules

actions.title: Canadian steel tariff-rate quotas (50% surtax above quota)
actions.rateNote: Over-quota surtax; quotas set at 50% of 2024 volumes for non-FTA countries and 100% for FTA partners; extra 25% on steel melted and poured in China

actions.title: Canadian counter-tariffs on C$27.6B of US goods in response to Section 338 (15%, 25%, 50%)
actions.rateNote: 50% on dairy, milk proteins, honey, plastics, wood, paper, textiles, glass, steel products, stoves; 25% on fresh cheese, lumber, carpets, appliance parts; 15% on the remainder — 629 tariff lines
actions.hsLabel: dairy, steel, appliances, farm equipment, furniture, pulp & paper, electronics
actions.notes: 'Dollar for dollar' response announced Aug 25, 2026 after US–Canada talks collapsed. The US answered with import bans effective Sept 29.

actions.title: Canadian 100% surtax on Chinese electric vehicles
actions.rateNote: From Jan 16, 2026 a quota of 49,000 vehicles/year (rising to ~70,000 over five years) enters at the 6.1% MFN rate; 100% above quota

actions.title: Canadian 25% surtax on Chinese steel and aluminum
actions.notes: Unchanged by the January 2026 Canada–China deal.

actions.title: Chinese retaliatory tariffs on ~$110B of US goods (2018–19 trade war)
actions.rateNote: 5–25% on soybeans, autos, LNG, chemicals and more; partly reduced/excluded under the Phase One deal

actions.title: Chinese tariffs on US coal, LNG (15%), crude oil, farm machinery and pickups (10%)
actions.hsLabel: coal, LNG, crude oil, agricultural machinery, pickup trucks
actions.notes: Response to the first 10% fentanyl tariff. Not covered by the November 2025 tariff cuts.

actions.title: Chinese tariffs on US agricultural goods (15% chicken, wheat, corn, cotton; 10% soybeans, pork, beef, dairy, fruit)
actions.hsLabel: meat, dairy, fruit, grains, soybeans, cotton
actions.notes: Lifted under the Busan arrangement in exchange for the US halving its fentanyl tariff.

actions.title: Chinese across-the-board tariff on US goods

rateHistory.note: Geneva truce; 24% suspended, extension to Nov 10, 2026

actions.notes: Still collected after the US reciprocal tariff was struck down; Beijing has said it will 'assess' US changes and has not added tariff countermeasures to the 2026 Section 301 forced-labor duty.

actions.title: Chinese tariffs on Canadian canola oil and meal, peas (100%), pork and seafood (25%)
actions.rateNote: From Mar 1, 2026 canola meal, peas, lobster and crab are tariff-free until at least end-2026; 100% on canola oil and 25% on pork and other seafood remain
actions.notes: Retaliation for Canada's 2024 EV and steel surtaxes.

actions.title: Chinese anti-dumping duty on Canadian canola seed
EU countervailing duties on Chinese battery electric vehicles
actions.rateNote: 7.8%–35.3% by producer, on top of the 10% MFN duty; five years

actions.title: EU countermeasures on €93B of US goods (suspended)
actions.rateNote: 4.4–30% on Annexes I–XIII of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1564; suspended before taking effect and kept suspended under the EU–US framework
actions.notes: The EU instead removed its tariffs on US industrial goods from July 1, 2026.

actions.title: EU steel overcapacity measure: 50% duty above tariff-rate quotas
actions.rateNote: Out-of-quota duty; quotas ~47% below the 2024 safeguard volumes; melt-and-pour origin proof from Oct 1, 2026
actions.notes: Regulation (EU) 2026/1384, replacing the steel safeguard that expired June 30, 2026.

actions.title: Mexican tariffs of up to 50% on 1,463 tariff lines from non-FTA countries
actions.rateNote: 5–50%; 50% on vehicles; autos, auto parts, steel, textiles, apparel, footwear, plastics, furniture, toys, aluminum, glass. Valid through Dec 31, 2026
actions.hsLabel: vehicles, steel, textiles, apparel, footwear, plastics, furniture
actions.notes: Published in the Diario Oficial on Dec 30, 2025. Applies at the MFN level, so it hits goods from countries without a trade agreement with Mexico.
